arxiv-2111-01510.title: A Hybrid Approach for Learning to Shift and Grasp with Elaborate Motion Primitives
arxiv-2111-01510.creator: Zohar Feldman, Hanna Ziesche, Ngo Anh Vien, Dotan Di Castro
arxiv-2111-01510.description: Abstract Many possible fields of application of robots in real world settings hinge on the ability of robots to grasp objects. As a result, robot grasping has been an active field of research for many years. With our publication we contribute to the endeavor of enabling robots to grasp, with a particular focus on bin picking applications.

arxiv-2112-09445.title: OTTER: Data Efficient Language-Supervised Zero-Shot Recognition with Optimal Transport Distillation
arxiv-2112-09445.creator: Bichen Wu, Ruizhe Cheng, Peizhao Zhang, Tianren Gao, Peter Vajda, Joseph E. Gonzalez
arxiv-2112-09445.description: Abstract Traditional computer vision models are trained to predict a fixed set of predefined categories. Recently, natural language has been shown to be a broader and richer source of supervision that provides finer descriptions to visual concepts than supervised "gold" labels.

arxiv-2207-06889.title: Nonreciprocal Amplification Transition in a Driven-Dissipative Quantum Network
arxiv-2207-06889.creator: Mingsheng Tian, Fengxiao Sun, Kaiye Shi, Haitan Xu, Qiongyi He, Wei Zhang
arxiv-2207-06889.description: Abstract We study the transport properties of a driven-dissipative quantum network, where multiple bosonic cavities such as photonic microcavities are coupled through a nonreciprocal bus with unidirectional transmission. For short-range coupling between the cavities, the occurrence of nonreciprocal amplification can be linked to a topological phase transition of the underlying dynamic Hamiltonian.

arxiv-2310-14818.title: Elementary catastrophes underlying bifurcations of vector fields and PDEs
arxiv-2310-14818.creator: Mike R. Jeffrey
arxiv-2310-14818.description: Abstract A practical method was proposed recently for finding local bifurcation points in an n n -dimensional vector field F F by seeking their ‘ underlying catastrophes ’. Here we apply the idea to the homogeneous steady states of a partial differential equation as an example of the role that catastrophes can play in reaction diffusion.

arxiv-2310-19804.description: Abstract Behavioural metrics have been shown to be an effective mechanism for constructing representations in reinforcement learning. We present a novel perspective on behavioural metrics for Markov decision processes via the use of positive definite kernels. We leverage this new perspective to define a new metric that is provably equivalent to the recently introduced MICo distance ( Castro et al.

arxiv-2311-17142.title: Transverse Energy-Energy Correlators in the Color-Glass Condensate at the Electron-Ion Collider
arxiv-2311-17142.creator: Zhong-Bo Kang, Jani Penttala, Fanyi Zhao, Yiyu Zhou
arxiv-2311-17142.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhong-Bo Kang, Jani Penttala, Fanyi Zhao, Yiyu Zhou. We investigate the transverse energy-energy correlators (TEEC) in the small- x x regime at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Focusing on the back-to-back production of electron-hadron pairs in both e ​ p ep and e ​ A eA collisions, we establish a factorization theorem given in terms of the hard function, quark distributions, soft functions, and TEEC jet functions, where the gluon saturation effect is incorporated.

arxiv-2412-07954.creator: Parsa Ghazvinian 1 , Robert Podschwadt 2 , Prajwal Panzade 1 , Mohammad H. Rafiei 3 and Daniel Takabi 2
arxiv-2412-07954.description: Abstract Due to the extensive application of machine learning (ML) in a wide range of fields and the necessity of data privacy, privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML) solutions have recently gained significant traction. One group of approaches relies on Homomorphic Encryption (HE), which enables us to perform ML tasks over encrypted data.

pmc-11383551.title: Hétérogénéité de l’identité noire : l’importance de l’intersectionnalité dans la recherche sur le racisme envers les personnes noires et l’équité des soins de santé au Canada

pmc-11383551.description: onnées montre que le racisme envers les personnes noires affecte la santé et le bien-être des populations noires au Canada. La question de l’hétérogénéité des expériences de racisme envers les personnes noires en soins de santé au Canada demeure insuffisamment étudiée.

pmc-11866054.title: Unilateral parotid gland double hemangiomas in an infant: A rare case report
pmc-11866054.creator: Francesco Toscano, Paolo Versace
pmc-11866054.description: Parotid hemangiomas, the most common salivary gland tumors in pediatric patients, are rare vascular tumors that typically present within the first year of life and are more common in females. We report the case of a 3-month-old female infant with a palpable, soft, noncompressible swelling at the right mandibular angle, which became more prominent in the evening.

pmc-12575322.title: Molecular mechanisms governing the differentiation and expansion of myeloid-derived suppressor cells
pmc-12575322.creator: Ke Wang, Xiao Wang, Nan Sun
pmc-12575322.description: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) play critical roles in tumor immune evasion. These heterogeneous cells are broadly classified into granulocytic (G-MDSC), monocytic (M-MDSC), and their immature precursors, early-stage MDSCs (e-MDSCs). Elucidating their differentiation and expansion mechanisms is crucial for advancing cancer immunotherapy. This review examines the key signaling pathways (e.g.

pmc-12716961.title: Development of a Machine Learning Model to Predict Epidural-Related Maternal Fever During Labor Analgesia: A Multi-Algorithm Comparative Study with Prospective Implementation Framework
pmc-12716961.creator: Guoxiu Zhang, Yihui Yang, Rugang An, Zhengquan Tan
pmc-12716961.description: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a machine learning-based predictive model for assessing the risk of epidural-related maternal fever (ERMF)- a common complication during labor analgesia.MethodsA prospective cohort study was conducted among 500 parturients with term singleton pregnancies who received epidural labor analgesia between September 2022 and August 2023.

pmc-13086340.title: Seroprevalence and altitude-dependent patterns of Toxoplasma gondii infection in livestock from northern Armenia
pmc-13086340.creator: Ruzanna Gevorgyan, Sargis A. Aghayan, Oleg Shcherbakov, Ahmad Daryani, Tigran Abgaryan, Hasmik Gevorgyan
pmc-13086340.description: Toxoplasmosis, caused by the intracellular protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, is a zoonotic disease affecting almost all warm-blooded vertebrates. Despite its importance to both humans and animals, research on toxoplasmosis in Armenia has been limited, with a notable 35-year gap in studies focused on host animals. This study aimed to conduct a survey of T. gondii seroprevalence among livestock in Armenia.

pmc-13162165.title: Dapagliflozin Protects Cardiomyocytes against Doxorubicin-Induced Toxicity by Modulating Sirtuin 1/Sirtuin 3 and Ferroptosis Pathway
pmc-13162165.creator: Hnin Ei Ei Khine, Supachoke Mangmool, Warisara Parichatikanond
pmc-13162165.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cardiac dysfunction can be aggravated by chemotherapeutic agents, including doxorubicin, through mechanisms involving mitochondrial dysfunction, elevated oxidative stress, suppression of sirtuin (SIRT1/SIRT3) signaling, and activation of apoptotic and ferroptotic pathways. Dapagliflozin, a selective sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, has been demonstrated to possess cardioprotective effects; however, the interplay between sirtuin signaling and ferroptosis in dapagliflozin-mediated cardioprotection under doxorubicin-induced stress remains unclear.

pmc-13227800.title: Blue light receptor phot2 collaborates with NRL-30 to negatively regulate immunity by reducing mitochondrial protein PRXIIF stability in potato
pmc-13227800.creator: Huishan Qiu, Yanli Liu, Tianyu Lin, Dong Cheng, Qingguo Sun, Xinya Wu, Lang Liu, Jiahui Nie, Mingshuo Fan, Jing Zhou, Ruimin Yu, Meng Xu, Qin He, Hongying Du, Zhendong Tian
pmc-13227800.description: Blue light (BL) receptor phototropins (phots) regulate numerous BL-induced physiological responses through NPH3/RPT2-like (NRL) family members. However, how phots and NRL proteins regulate plant immunity remain incompletely understood. This study demonstrates that Stphot2 negatively regulated resistance against Phytophthora infestans, the causal agent of late blight, in potato and Nicotiana benthamiana.

pmc-13391495.title: A universal scaling law for active diffusion in complex media
pmc-13391495.creator: Qun Zhang, Yuxin Tian, Xue Zhang, Xiaoting Yu, Hongwei Zhu, Ning Zheng, Luhui Ning, Ran Ni, Mingcheng Yang, Peng Liu
pmc-13391495.description: Understanding how active particles transport in structurally heterogeneous environments is a fundamental and challenging problem, with relevance to biological and synthetic microswimmers in tissues and porous media. Here, using granular experiments and computer simulations, we investigate the long-time diffusion of active tracers in quasi-two-dimensional heterogeneous media.

pmc-13593231.title: Hematological parameters as predictors of prostate cancer: A study based on multivariable and bidirectional Mendelian randomization
pmc-13593231.creator: Yirui Wei, Hao Wang, Liang Wang, Pushen Yang, Dawei Xie, Weifeng He, Jianwen Wang
pmc-13593231.description: This study explores the causal relationship between hematologic parameters and prostate cancer (PCa) risk, offering insights into potential biological pathways and clinical implications. We used genome-wide association studies to perform forward and reverse Mendelian randomization (MR) within a 2-sample framework. Additionally, multivariable MR was employed to assess the associations between multiple hematological markers and PCa.

pmc-13605220.title: Tumor Acidosis Boosts Antibody-Driven Cytotoxic Potential of Neutrophils
pmc-13605220.creator: Tosca Holtrop, Ida C. van der Peet, Ilona S. T. Hendriks, Tineke Kardol-Hoefnagel, Robin B. Schol, Marta Lustig, Kevin Budding, Jeanette H. W. Leusen, Patricia A. Olofsen, Maria Tsioumpekou

What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13680515.title: Efficient enzyme-mediated degradation of various emerging pollutants, including 2-mercaptobenzothiazole, paracetamol, and sulfamethoxazole, using HRP@UiO-66-NH2
pmc-13680515.creator: Khadega A. Al-Maqdi, Shaikha Alneyadi, Nada Elmerhi, Lamia A. Siddig, Ahmed Alzamly, Iltaf Shah, Syed Salman Ashraf
pmc-13680515.description: The increasing contamination of water sources due to industrialization and population growth poses significant environmental and health risks, even at trace pollutant concentrations. Enzymatic bioremediation, particularly using horseradish peroxidase (HRP), has shown great potential in pollutant degradation due to its high selectivity and catalytic efficiency. However, limitations such as poor operational stability and reusability hinder its large-scale application.
